events.event: The IHSG closed down 1.02% at 5,194.14 on 19 November, a second straight day of losses after Bank Indonesia's rate hike, with CNBC Indonesia also citing hawkish Fed minutes.
events.key_numbers: Close 5,194.14 (-53.74 pts, -1.02%) · open 5,232.39 · intraday low 5,152.41 · value Rp7.42 trillion · 216.54 million lots · previous close 5,247.88 (18 Nov)
events.why_it_matters: The index is sliding back toward 5,100 even after BI raised rates to defend the rupiah, which hits stock investors' portfolios.
events.spreading_evidence: Covered by CNBC Indonesia, RRI, Suara, Balipost and others

events.event: The rupiah closed weaker at Rp18,254 per US dollar on 19 November, reversing part of the previous day's gain after the BI rate hike, while foreigners net sold big bank stocks.
events.key_numbers: Rupiah Rp18,254/USD (-0.12%) · previous close Rp18,232 (18 Nov) · foreign net sell BBRI ~Rp322.77 billion · BMRI ~Rp145.42 billion · TLKM ~Rp126.97 billion · BI Rate 6.00% (+25 bps)
events.why_it_matters: A rate hike did not stop the rupiah from weakening, so imports, fuel and loan costs stay under pressure.

events.event: Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting showed concern about inflation and the possibility of rate hikes of up to 50 basis points, per CNBC Indonesia.
events.key_numbers: Fed funds range 3.75%-4.00% (per Owrite) · possible hike up to 50 bps · UK October inflation 3.6% y/y · Japan October trade deficit JPY476.5 billion
events.why_it_matters: A Fed leaning toward hikes strengthens the dollar and makes it harder for the rupiah to recover.
